page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network performance is a key feature, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a strong multi-core performance profile alongside moderate single-core capabilities. The instance achieved a strong multi-core score of 97017.01 in stress-ng and a strong software compilation score of 42663.0 in Geekbench using Clang. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is highly efficient at 3782.81 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to average levels of 166.91 GB/sec and 74.46 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, show weaker performance, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to leverage the 64 physical cores effectively.

This instance is highly suited for network-intensive, multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, which demonstrated a strong throughput of 44.93 GB/sec, and high-throughput database operations, as evidenced by a strong Redis SET performance of 72.72 million operations per second. However, it is poorly suited for large language model inference, where text generation speeds for a medium 7B model reach only 20.48 tokens per second and drop to 2.73 tokens per second for a large 70B model. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration further limits its utility for heavy data science or direct disk-bound database workloads, making it a specialized choice for network-heavy compute tasks.
